sections.heading: 正文
paragraphs: Experience is not a complete copy of reality. It is a workable version formed under limits of attention, memory, representation, and action. In “Why Responsibility and Identity Become Unstable: Commitment, Agency, and Identity Compression,” the useful task is to trace how Responsibility Formation changes the present configuration, how the intermediate mechanisms select or stabilize what can be carried forward, and how Identity Drift creates conditions that the next cycle of runtime may inherit.

This continuity matters because consciousness, emotion, self-model, and action are not merely neighboring labels. What becomes visible changes what can be evaluated; what repeats influences prediction and selection; what stabilizes may later become either support or inertia. The deeper question is how these mechanisms hand conditions to one another and where feedback still allows the runtime to reorganize.

sections.heading: Responsibility Formation
paragraphs: Responsibility and commitment extend a momentary choice across time. They require continued allocation of effort, repair, and consequence; when capacity or context shifts, agency can weaken and an old commitment may need to be re-aligned with present conditions.

Placed back into the larger runtime chain, this mechanism both inherits a prior state and changes the conditions from which the next state can form. It does not determine an entire person or relationship by itself. Its significance is relational: it changes what is easier to notice, stabilize, express, coordinate, or act upon, and therefore must be read together with inputs, current configuration, feedback, and adjacent mechanisms.

sections.heading: Identity Compression
paragraphs: A finite carrier cannot preserve every detail of reality at once. Compression keeps selected differences and relations while discarding background complexity, making experience portable and recallable but ensuring that internal representation never equals the full environment.

sections.heading: Identity Drift
paragraphs: Self and identity can be understood as continuity models assembled across memory, role, responsibility, and expectation. They reduce coordination cost by stabilizing answers to who is acting and what matters, yet the same stability can become inertia when the surrounding reality has already changed.

Placed back into the larger runtime chain, this mechanism both inherits a prior state and changes the conditions from which the next state can form. It does not determine an entire person or relationship by itself. Its significance is relational: it changes what is easier to notice, stabilize, express, coordinate, or act upon, and therefore must be read together with inputs, current configuration, feedback, and adjacent mechanisms.

sections.heading: From Responsibility Formation to Identity Drift
paragraphs: Read together, these mechanisms describe a transition rather than a random collection of topics. Responsibility Formation establishes the starting condition; Commitment Stability and Agency Collapse reorganize what the runtime can carry; Identity Compression pushes the configuration into a different operating layer; and Identity Drift shows what becomes available as a consequence. The sequence makes the relation between prior and later states easier to trace.

Real systems do not always move through these mechanisms in a clean five-step order. Some processes run in parallel, some feedback travels backward, and a runtime may remain fixed around one transition for a long period. The purpose is not to manufacture a universal formula, but to reconnect the mechanisms into a chain that can be compared, traced, and tested against a concrete reality.

sections.heading: Reading the mechanisms as one runtime chain
paragraphs: These mechanisms are not five independent definitions. Each is a view onto a continuous sequence in which an earlier state changes the inputs available to the next, while later outcomes return through feedback and alter future selection. The useful question is therefore not whether a label is present, but where continuity is being lost, where a configuration has become overly fixed, and where reconfiguration remains possible.

Seen together, runtime becomes traceable rather than mysterious: what entered, what stabilized, what was amplified, what was compressed, what travelled through relationship, and what changed after feedback. This map does not replace case evidence or professional judgment. It provides a structured way to locate the mechanisms that a concrete case would still need to verify.
